overview.text: The Eastern Massasauga is a small rattlesnake of eastern North America, around the Great Lakes. It is the only venomous snake in Ontario, Canada.

identification.text: Grey or tan with a row of big, rounded dark blotches down the back and smaller spots along the sides. Some are completely black.

distribution.label: Native
distribution.text: Southern Ontario in Canada and the Great Lakes region and eastern Midwest of the United States.

habitat.text: Wetlands - swamps, marshes, bogs, fens, wet meadows and floodplains - often using crayfish burrows. In summer some move to drier ground.

diet.text: Small animals: mostly voles, mice and shrews for adults, while young ones often eat lizards or snakes; frogs, birds and even centipedes are also taken.

reproduction.text: Gives birth to live young, usually in August or September - about 5 to 14 at a time. Females usually breed only every second year.

recognise.text: Small rattlesnake with a rattle on the tail.
Large dark blotches down a grey or tan back.
